summary: A note on the cost of network software, using the survey mechanisms that hosts use to see who is up as an example of wasted overhead. MIT-DMCG and UCLA-NMC agreed on a standard format for host survey data and would make it available, so others need not poll. The title is a quote from complaints.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 425 proposes that a few sites collect host-status information and share it in a common format. Other sites could use those results instead of repeatedly checking hosts themselves.

subtitle: A shared host-status service to reduce repeated network surveys

tldr.problem: Many sites independently surveyed hosts to see which were up, creating network traffic and system overhead.
tldr.mechanism: MIT-DMCG and UCLA-NMC agreed on a concise standard format for survey results and planned to make the information available through a standard socket.
tldr.outcome: Other sites were asked to stop surveying independently and obtain data from an official surveyor when needed or periodically.

today: RFC 425 proposes a shared host-survey service to reduce duplicated network traffic. It says the precise format and socket number would be announced later.

sections.title: The Cost of Repeated Surveys
sections.content:
The RFC notes that network users were beginning to measure the cost of network software and use. It identifies repeated host surveys, used to learn which systems were available, as a source of overhead that was not charged to a particular user.

Several systems had found that surveying alone accounted for a significant part of their overhead.
sections.plainLanguage: Many sites repeatedly checked which hosts were available. These checks used network and computer resources without being assigned to a particular user.

sections.title: A Shared Survey Result Format
sections.content:
MIT-DMCG and UCLA-NMC agreed on a standard format for host survey data and planned to make it available to the network community. The data would be a concise character stream that people and programs could read. A third site was expected to join, and the group planned to provide a standard socket for obtaining the information.

The exact data format and socket number were still forthcoming.
sections.plainLanguage: A small group planned to publish host-status results in a concise common format. The notice says the exact format and socket number had not yet been announced.

sections.title: Using Official Surveyors
sections.content: The authors intended other sites to stop running their own surveys and obtain results from an official surveyor, either when a user asked or on a schedule. They also urge sites to consider the cost of network traffic and avoid repeated interactions with a host without expressed consent, such as an account number or a specific experiment.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites were asked to use shared survey results instead of checking hosts on their own. The authors also ask users to consider the cost of repeated traffic to another host.
